learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the fundamentals of static and electromechanical conversion systems.

Learn the configuration of basic power electronic conversion systems, of main electrical machines, either direct current (DC) or alternate current (AC) and of electric drives used in automotive sector.
Learn topology, control principles, input and output characteristics of main DC and AC electric drives.
Develop the ability to model power electronic converters, control system, electrical machines, and full drive systems with reference to application for torque and speed control.
Develop the ability to represent an electric drive in terms of energetic conversion system, for the integration in a multiphisic model of a vehicle.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of electromechanical conversion systems and fundamentals of electrical machines.
Revision of electromagnetic fields and EM field equations.
Revision on ferromagnetic materials and permanent magnets.
Topology and types of DC machines.
Fundamental equations and output mechanical characteristic.
Drives on one, two, four quadrants.
Brushless machines with trapezoidal back emf.
Brushless machine with sinusoidal back emf.
Structure of the machine with surface and internal mount magnets.
Introduction to Clarke and Park coordinate transformation.
One, two and four quadrant configuration.
Modelling of a Complete Electric Drive in Simulink
Development of a complete electric drive model, including the electrical machine, power electronic converter, PWM modulation, current and speed controllers, and mechanical load.

Analysis of four-quadrant operation in the torque
–speed plane, electrical and mechanical operating characteristics, and basic sizing criteria for motion control, automation, and automotive applications.
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of a project and an oral examination. The project involves developing a computer model of an electric drive, to be presented at the examination. The oral examination includes a presentation and discussion of the project, and an assessment of theoretical knowledge through discussion and calculations. The final grade is weighted 50% for the project report and 50% for the oral examination.
